# Camouflare 1.4.0

> Draft for maintainer review. Remove this note before publishing the GitHub Release.

Camouflare 1.4.0 keeps the browser pool warm without waiting for traffic, stops the
readiness probe from queueing behind live requests, ships a reproducible service
benchmark runner with recorded evidence for the published image, and narrows the
production Compose profile to one isolated context per browser.

## What changed

- A browser retired by `BROWSER_MAX_USES` or `BROWSER_MAX_AGE_MINUTES` is replaced in
  the background as soon as it closes, and a periodic tick
  (`POOL_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 15) retires aged idle browsers and
  relaunches to `POOL_MIN_BROWSERS`. Background launches wait for closing browsers, so
  the tick never runs more than `POOL_MAX_BROWSERS` processes.
- `GET /ready` returns HTTP 200 with `capacity_state: "saturated"` when every context
  slot is held by a browser that is still serving, instead of waiting for a probe slot
  and reporting 503. Disconnected browsers are retired before that verdict, so a dead
  busy browser is still probed. A 503 now means the pool could not produce a working
  browser. The readiness metric records these probes under `result="saturated"`.
- Production Compose limits each browser to one concurrent context. A load run against
  the 1.3.3 image completed 45 of 45 requests with isolated contexts, while the previous
  two-context profile timed out two requests in one of five four-client rounds.
- `scripts/benchmark_service.py` writes schema 2 JSON evidence with a machine-readable
  acceptance block; three 2026-08-25 runs are recorded under `docs/benchmarks/`.
- README, the deployment guide, and `/documentation` now describe the real pool
  semantics: one concurrent persistent session in the shipped profile, the acquire wait
  as the earlier of `POOL_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS` and `maxTimeout`, every pool and browser
  recycle setting, and the direct-HTTP GET preflight for `ajax=true` requests.

## Upgrading

- The shipped Compose profile now allows one concurrent persistent session (two context
  slots, one reserved for stateless traffic). A second `sessions.create` returns HTTP 503
  `POOL_UNAVAILABLE` immediately. Raise `POOL_MAX_BROWSERS` after load testing memory
  and PID usage, or set `POOL_RESERVED_TRANSIENT_CONTEXTS=0`, to restore capacity.
- `POOL_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` is new and defaults to 15 seconds; it must be
  greater than zero.
- `/ready` may now return a 200 body with `capacity_state` and `message` in addition to
  `status`. Clients that only read `status` are unaffected; the OpenAPI schema declares
  the optional fields. Readiness alerts should treat 503 as "no working browser", not
  "busy".
- Successful `/v1` responses are unchanged.

## Container image

The immutable release image is available for Linux `amd64` and `arm64`:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/mehmetcansahin/camouflare:1.4.0
```

See the
[changelog](https://github.com/mehmetcansahin/camouflare/blob/v1.4.0/CHANGELOG.md#140---2026-08-26)
for the complete entry and the
[deployment guide](https://github.com/mehmetcansahin/camouflare/blob/v1.4.0/docs/deployment.md)
for production constraints and rollback guidance.
